restrained-satire.voice_reason: Z, like 《药》, lets irony come from flat juxtaposed physical detail and silent officials (the unanswered window, the weighed envelope, the dust mark on the bench, the sleeve tug) with almost no narrator comment, whereas X keeps stepping in with explanatory similes and a closing aphorism that tells the reader what the satire means.
restrained-satire.notes: V, X and Y are near-copies of one draft: X = V plus two extra commentary lines; Y trims V's sentimental fingertip passage and the shoe-nail visit but pastes 『』 quotation marks from the reference while keeping “” elsewhere, an inconsistent surface mimicry. V and Y are nearly indistinguishable in voice. The timing violation shared by V/W/X/Y is mild but real: the material's 下班前 makes the substitution happen after the old man is gone, which these drafts replace with an on-the-spot choice he witnesses; Z alone keeps it. W is the closest to Z in cold juxtaposition (the 11-second 大妈 thanked before speaking, the framed zeros neater than his own).
